title: The Borrowed Book with a Deadline
scene: Two friends discuss a borrowed novel that one of them hasn't finished.
sceneJa: 友人に借りた小説をまだ読み終えていない。返却を延ばしてほしいが、相手にも予定があるので、まず必要な日を確認する。

chunks.en: but could I hang on to your book
chunks.ja: 君の本をもう少し借りていてもいいかな、
まだ半分しか読めていなくて、
結末をじっくり楽しみたいんだ。
基本的には大丈夫だけど、

chunks.en: but I promised to lend it to my sister
chunks.ja: 妹にも貸す約束をしていて、

chunks.en: When do you need it back
chunks.ja: いつまでに返せばいい、

chunks.en: If you can return it by Friday,
chunks.ja: 金曜日までに返してくれるなら、

chunks.en: and she can pick it up Saturday.
chunks.ja: 土曜日に妹が取りに来られるから。
融通を利かせてくれてありがとう。

chunks.en: I'll drop it off on Friday
rather than leave it to the last minute.
chunks.ja: ぎりぎりにならないように。

questions.question: Which split keeps the request as a natural chunk?
options: could I / hang on / to your book
could I hang on to your book / for a couple more days?
could / I hang / on to your book
questions.explanation: Hang on to something means keep it; the full request works as one meaningful unit.

questions.question: What does 'at the latest' mean?
questions.explanation: At the latest sets the final acceptable time.

questions.question: Why does the friend ask when the book is needed back?
options: To avoid assuming an extension is possible and agree on a clear deadline.
To complain that the novel is boring.
To suggest the sister should buy a copy.
questions.explanation: The speaker checks the other person's constraint before making a promise.

speak: In 30 seconds, ask a friend to keep something you borrowed for two more days. Ask when they need it back at the latest, and agree on a specific return day.
review: New: I hate to ask（頼みにくいけれど）, hang on to（手元に置いておく）, at the latest（遅くとも）. Review: I'd rather ...（〜の方がいい）, That works for me（それで大丈夫）.
